Commentary & Market Overview
Final Close

items: Guggenheim Investments Private Debt Fund IV (‘PDF IV’ or ‘The Fund’) held its final close on March 31, 2026. The Fund closed on $4.5 billion in commitments, achieving its hard cap and notably surpassing the initial fundraise target of $3.0 billion.

blocks.text: Market Backdrop

items: In 2024 and 2025, 86% of all capital raised in non-traded BDCs was concentrated among just five managers. In 2024, $35.5 billion of capital was raised from the retail channel in non-traded BDCs, with the largest non-traded BDC capturing nearly one-third of inflows at ~$11 billion and the top five managers collectively accounting for approximately $30.7 billion of the total amount raised1.

Retail investor sentiment has changed due to concerns about lower interest rates, AI impact on software, and higher than expected default rates. Retail investor outflows have followed with redemption requests at the five largest non-traded BDCs exceeding the 5% quarterly limit with some BDCs seeing redemption requests at up to 40% of total fund NAV2.

Non-traded BDCs have significantly lowered their hold size in deals and have reduced appetite for deals in the software sector. This reduced competition should lead to better pricing, documentation, and LTV in private credit transactions if redemption requests persist.

blocks.text: PDF IV Recent Activity

items: Consistent with our process over the last 20+ years, we remain focused on finding compelling relative value in fundamentally sound companies.

Market volatility, particularly in February, due to AI concerns impacted the software and tech adjacent names. The market partially recovered in March, but software loans and tech adjacent loans were impacted. As a result, software loans and tech adjacent loans were marked down an average of 1.21% and 0.16% respectively in Q1 2026.

Three loans are currently electing PIK alongside cash coupon (all of which was designed PIK at origination which sunset over time). PIK as a percentage of net investment income in PDF IV remains less than 3%, compared to 24.8% PIK as a share of net investment income among a composite of the 13 largest US BDCs3.

Inspired Pet has been added to the low alert and monitor list given leverage and underlying trends. Total leverage has increased over 1.0x since deal time. The deal team has a meeting with management the week of June 8th to gain a deeper understanding of drivers of the softer performance.

PDF IV closed three deals in 1Q26. Since the end of the first quarter, PDF IV has closed an additional three deals since and has signed an additional three deals which have not yet closed. The six closed deals represent $668mm of dollars committed at a weighted average spread of SOFR + 546 basis points with first lien net leverage of 4.0x, a blended LTV of 42% and meaningful downside and structural protections in each of these deals.
Please see the enclosed case studies for additional information on the deals closed in 1Q26.
